design.objective: Make duplicate-application confirmation a single collection-level action that closes immediately and is requested again only when conflict facts change.
users: Release applicants submitting a new application that overlaps an existing application in the same production window

requirements.statement: The create-new confirmation must appear as the primary footer action beside defer handling.
acceptance: The footer renders defer first and create-new second with primary styling
counterexample: Create-new remains inside each historical-application card

requirements.statement: Confirming create-new must close the dialog immediately and submit with the current conflict token without duplicate clicks.
acceptance: The dialog closes before the submit request finishes
The submit request contains the confirmed token
counterexample: The dialog remains visible after confirmation
A second click starts another submit

requirements.statement: An unchanged confirmed conflict must not reopen the dialog; only a changed server token may require confirmation again.
acceptance: A same-token 409 shows its actual error with the dialog closed
A changed-token 409 refreshes facts and reopens the dialog
requirements.source: User correction and approved recommended design on 2026-08-18
counterexample: Every 409 is treated as a duplicate conflict

requirements.statement: Existing cancel-old, edit-old and defer actions must remain compatible.
acceptance: Card-level cancel and edit remain available according to allowedActions
requirements.source: Existing behavior preserved by user-approved bounded fix
counterexample: The fix removes or changes existing card-level actions

invariants: No unrelated dirty-worktree change is overwritten
Existing permission and application-state rules remain unchanged
constraints: Modify only the two authorized Vue files
Reuse Vue 3 and Element Plus patterns
Do not change API, backend, schema or dependencies
non_goals: Persisting conflict confirmation across page reloads

selected_approach.name: Transient confirmed conflict token with direct submit
selected_approach.reason: The submit API already validates the token, so this removes the redundant create-new resolution round trip and distinguishes changed conflicts from unrelated 409 responses.

alternatives.name: Persist confirmation on the backend
alternatives.rejected_because: It requires schema and lifecycle changes beyond this defect.

alternatives.name: Only close the dialog
alternatives.rejected_because: The broad 409 handler would still reopen it.

components.name: ReleaseConflictDialog
components.responsibility: Render conflict facts, card-specific actions and one collection-level create-new confirmation.

components.name: ReleaseManagementPrototype
components.responsibility: Retain the confirmed token for the current pending application and route submit outcomes correctly.

interfaces.name: choose event
interfaces.contract: CREATE_NEW is collection-level and carries no historical item; CANCEL_OLD and EDIT_OLD carry the selected historical item.

interfaces.name: submit conflictToken
interfaces.contract: A token confirms exactly the currently observed conflict facts; a different returned token requires new confirmation.

data_flows.input: User confirms create-new with current conflict report
transitions: compare token only if submit returns 409
data_flows.output: Application enters review, actual non-conflict error is shown, or changed conflicts are reopened

error_handling.condition: Submission returns 409 with unchanged conflict token
error_handling.behavior: Keep the conflict dialog closed and show the original business error.
error_handling.recovery: User resolves the reported business issue and retries within the current application context.

error_handling.condition: Submission returns 409 with a changed conflict token
error_handling.behavior: Refresh the application and conflict report, clear prior confirmation and reopen the dialog.
error_handling.recovery: User reviews the changed facts and confirms again.

security: No permission or identity behavior changes
performance: CREATE_NEW removes one redundant resolution request
compatibility: Existing API and card actions remain compatible
operations: Actual submission errors remain visible instead of being masked as duplicate conflicts

verification_strategy.signal: Footer order and immediate close are visible and one submit request carries the token.
verification_strategy.method: Desktop browser interaction plus request observation.

verification_strategy.signal: Same-token errors do not reopen, changed-token errors do, and existing actions remain.
verification_strategy.method: Focused code contract, production build and browser regression.

assumptions.text: The existing conflict token changes whenever conflict facts relevant to confirmation change.
assumptions.basis: The backend recomputes and compares the token before submission.
assumptions.falsifier: A relevant conflict fact changes while the returned token remains identical.

decisions.decision: Use the existing token as a transient confirmation and reopen only on token change.
decisions.reason: It directly addresses both reported defects without backend changes.
decisions.source: User approved the recommended design and requested development on 2026-08-18.

risks.risk: An unrelated 409 may previously have been hidden behind the conflict dialog.
risks.impact: After the fix a real business error becomes visible.
risks.mitigation: Use apiErrorMessage and keep the saved draft available for correction.

approval.evidence: The user approved the recommended footer and token-comparison design by replying '开发'.

global_constraints: Modify only the two authorized Vue files
Do not change API, backend, database, permissions or dependencies
Do not commit, push or switch branches

file_map.responsibility: Conflict facts, card actions and dialog footer confirmation
Pending submission, confirmed token and submit error routing

tasks.goal: Correct duplicate-application confirmation layout and state flow.
input_facts: Backend submission accepts unchanged conflict facts when the token matches
Current frontend reopens conflicts for every HTTP 409

steps.action: Move CREATE_NEW to the dialog footer and make its conflict item optional.
steps.expected: Footer renders defer then primary create-new; cards retain cancel and edit only.

steps.action: Store the confirmed token, close immediately and submit directly.
steps.expected: One token-bearing submit starts while the dialog is closed and duplicate clicks are disabled.
steps.evidence: Focused diff and browser network/state observation

steps.action: Reopen only when the latest server conflict token differs from the confirmed token.
steps.expected: Same-token errors remain visible without reopening; changed tokens reopen with refreshed facts.
steps.evidence: Focused diff and controlled browser outcomes

steps.action: Run build, governance, scope, whitespace and browser verification.
steps.expected: Build succeeds and all acceptance paths are observable or explicitly disclosed.

acceptance_checks: Dialog closes immediately and submit carries token
risks: Dirty untracked release files require minimal patches
tasks.rollback: Restore only the changed sections of the two Vue files to their T1 pre-change content.
stop_conditions: The fix requires backend or API contract changes
The runtime cannot produce a duplicate conflict after three setup attempts
escalation_conditions: Confirmation must persist across page reloads
A new shared error code is required

integration_checks.expected: Footer, close, token submit and reopen rules match R1-R4 without console errors

approval.evidence: The user reviewed the recommended implementation behavior and replied '开发'.

plant_boundary_candidates: Release duplicate-conflict dialog and submit state flow

assumptions.text: The conflict token represents all relevant conflict facts.
assumptions.falsifier: Relevant facts change without a token change.
